To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the α1-subunit of L-type Ca2+-channels contains two functionally distinct Ca2+-binding sites in its voltage sensor and that the drug binding site is located in the S5-S6 linker between domains I and II.
the pore-forming subunit of voltage-gated Ca2+-channels is composed of a single polypeptide chain that is organized in four homologous repeats.

(i) the primary structure of the α1-subunit determines various functional properties of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels, (ii) the α1-sub-unit contains a pore-forming region that is highly homologous to the pore-forming region of Na+- and K+-channels and (iii) the pore-forming domain of the L-type Ca2+-channel is a target for clinically relevant Ca2+ channel blockers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular properties of voltage-gated Ca2+-channels and their role in cellular Ca2+-homeostasis and signal transduction.
the molecular structure and function of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels and their modulation.
the elucidation of structure-function relationships of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels and their regulation by drugs and toxins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the molecular properties of Ca2+-channels have become increasingly well understood, but that the complexity of the channel structure and its regulation by a variety of different factors still leaves room for further exciting and challenging research.
the molecular properties of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels are still not completely understood.
the molecular structure of Ca2+-channel subunits has been elucidated to a great extent, but that many details still need to be worked out.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α1-subunit is a complex protein with a modular organization.
the molecular properties of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels are now well understood.
the molecular properties of Ca2+-channels are now well understood at the level of primary structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pore region of L-type Ca2+-channel α1-subunits is structurally related to the pore-forming domains of voltage-gated Na+ and K+ channels.
the Ca2+-channel complex consists of a number of functionally distinct subunits.
the pore-forming subunit of voltage-gated Ca2+-channels consists of four homologous repeat domains.
